build: PAL original, two-sided G64; level 1 load in play

comments.text: [carry] For slot X (object Y), when no hit has been scored yet this frame ($10B0, $10B1), the player is striking ($5BBA or $5B2C set) and the slot is in state 1, 2, 14 or 15: compares the slot's height ($A3,X) with the player's ($747C) (10 lines above or $18 below) and its distance across with $747B, on the side the player faces ($59B9). On a hit it pushes the object 9 pixels away along the map unless it is past its limit ($0C9E-$0D97), sets the slot to state 1 (player facing right) or 2 (facing left), starts the hurt timer $0A86 with 10, sets $10B0 and $10B1 and calls $61AC.

[carry] Per-frame object update, skipped while the game is paused ($6443). Goes through the 11 slots: a slot in state 7 is only queued in the list at $1206; for the others, while the raster is above line $B4, it runs the player-attack test $10B2 and then the behaviour for the slot's state, through the table at $128B and a call whose operand is rewritten at $125F/$1260. The queued state 7 slots are then handled by $1D3E.
[carry] Sets the eight sprite pointers in both screens' tables ($CFF8-$CFFF and $CBF8-$CBFF) to X, X+1, up to X+7.
[carry] Draws the seven digits from $0A00 on into the panel's character shapes at $FA58 (8 bytes each from the digit shapes at $58C2) through $589C.
[carry] Copies the 8-byte shape of digit $0A00+X from $58C2 to the pointer $85/$86 and moves the pointer on 8 bytes.

[carry] Called from $6480 each frame. Unless the game is paused ($6443) it saves the player position in $5923/$5924 and runs the routine for the player's state $5912 (table at $5913, through a call whose operand is rewritten at $5948/$5949); it then draws the player's frames with $6111.
[carry] Fills with $FF the entries of the sorted sprite list at $0010 that each of the 11 slots used last frame (their positions are in $02-$0C).

[carry] Writes the player's three sprite pointers into both screens' tables ($CFF8-$CFFA and $CBF8-$CBFA) from the frame numbers in $610D-$6110, with different arrangements for states 2-4 and for the punch, crouch and strike.

[carry] Called by the hit test $10B2 with X the slot and Y the object. Takes 2 (when $10B1 is set) or 1 from the object's energy $0BA5 and adds 4 to the score digit 5; at zero energy it sets the slot and object to state $10, $0B00 to $FE and adds 8 to the score digit 5.
[carry] Sets the screen matrix bits of $D018 to $30 (screen at $CC00) when $2067 is zero and to $20 ($C800) when it is not, keeping the other bits.

[carry] Raster interrupt 2 of 3, on line $C5 (set by $6480). Moves sprites 3-7 to line $0A and clears their pointers, turns sprites off, sets $D018 and $D011 for the panel with extended colour mode, counts down $5577 and $1658, reads joystick port 2 ($DC00,$DC01) into $2064 and $2065 unless the recoil counter $1658 is running, sets the character set bits of $D018 to 8, runs the countdown $759B and the list clear $6088, and toggles $63E7. It sets line $CD and the vector $63E8 for the next interrupt.
[carry] Moves sprite 0 or sprite 1 by 8 pixels along X while the punch timer $5BBA or the strike timer $5B2C runs, to the right when the player faces right ($59B9 zero) and to the left otherwise.

[carry] Reads the keyboard with CIA 1 into A. Returns $FF at once when any of the low five bits of $DC00 AND $DC01 reads low (the test at $8F4D, so while the joystick or a key in that range is down); otherwise scans the eight rows from $8F5B, looks the key up in the table at $8FBF and returns its code. $2127 keeps the result in $8F44.

[carry] When the flag $6808 is set, clears it and copies the colours from the buffer at $7173-$7289 to colour RAM $D9E0-$DAF6, leaving out the last column of some rows. The second half of the colour update that $6809 starts.

[carry] Wipes the screen: sets the wipe flag $74BA and the pause flag $6443, then clears both screen matrices ($CC00 and $C800) in diagonal lines, each line stepping 39 characters from its start with the lengths taken from $747D, a delay through $655A after each, and clears the pause flag at the end. Called at the end of a level, by the game over screen and on the NMI exit.
[carry] Pause: when the key code in $8F44 is $50, sets $6443, waits for the key to be released, pressed again and released, then clears $6443.
[carry] Draws the three timer digits into the panel's character shapes at $F9F0, $F9E8 and $F9D8 through $7585.

[carry] Called from $6315 every frame unless the game is paused. When the three timer digits are zero it clears $0A10 and sets $760E to 1; otherwise on every second call it counts the digits down by one.
[carry] Called by the main loop. When $760E is 1 it sets it to 2 and runs $7678, which replaces the timer's graphics in the panel.
Sprite shapes for pointers $80 to $8F (1,024 bytes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's player_shapes_a.

Sprite shapes for pointers $90 to $93 (256 bytes), part of the player's punch and crouch frames: frame_b ($610E) takes $90 and $91 from punch_frames and $92 and $93 from crouch_frames. [carry] Same bytes as level 2's player_shapes_b.
Sprite shapes for pointers $94 to $96 (192 bytes): the player climbing, picked by climb_frames_up ($5FB1) and climb_frames_down ($5FBD). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's climb_shapes.
Sprite shapes for pointers $97 to $9C (384 bytes): the player walking right (walk_frames_right at $5964). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's walk_right_shapes.

Sprite shapes for pointers $9D to $A2 (384 bytes): the player walking left (walk_frames_left at $5952), drawn like walk_right_shapes, with $AA to $AF and $86 to $8B as the other two sprites. [carry] Same bytes as level 2's walk_left_shapes.
Sprite shapes for pointers $A3 to $B2 (1,024 bytes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's attack_shapes.

Sprite shapes for pointers $B3 to $C1 (960 bytes), the rest of attack_shapes: $B4 to $B7, $BB and $BE to $C1 are named there, and $B8 to $BA are the second sprite of the player climbing (F + $24, see climb_shapes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's attack_shapes_b.
Sprite shapes for pointers $C2 to $C4 (192 bytes): the third sprite of the player climbing (F + $2E, see climb_shapes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's shapes_unreferenced.

The status panel's bitmap, which the raster interrupt irq_bottom switches on from line $CD (bitmap mode at $E000, multicolour): 40 cells wide, rows 19 to 24, 8 bytes a cell and 320 a row. [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap.

Row 19, columns 32 to 37: the first of five rows of the 6 by 5 cell picture that timer_graphics_on ($760F) or timer_graphics_off ($7678) copies in (48 bytes a row; the others are panel_picture_1 to 4). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_picture_0.
Row 19, columns 38 and 39, and row 20, columns 0 to 26: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (232 bytes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_1.
Row 20, columns 27 to 31 (40 bytes): draw_timer ($755D) draws the three timer digits into the cells at $F9D8, $F9E8 and $F9F0. [carry] Same bytes as level 2's timer_cells.
Row 20, columns 32 to 37: the second row of the panel picture (see panel_picture_0). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_picture_1.
Row 20, columns 38 and 39, and row 21, columns 0 to 2: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (40 bytes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_2.
Row 21, columns 10 to 16: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (56 bytes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_3.
Row 21, columns 25 to 31: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (56 bytes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_4.
Row 21, columns 32 to 37: the third row of the panel picture (see panel_picture_0). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_picture_2.
Row 21, columns 38 and 39, and row 22, columns 0 to 31: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (272 bytes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_5.
Row 22, columns 32 to 37: the fourth row of the panel picture (see panel_picture_0). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_picture_3.
Row 22, columns 38 and 39, and row 23, columns 0 to 31: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (272 bytes). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_6.
Row 23, columns 32 to 37: the fifth row of the panel picture (see panel_picture_0). [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_picture_4.
Row 23, columns 38 and 39, and all of row 24 (336 bytes): panel bitmap that no traced routine writes. [carry] Same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_7.
